newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp to take brunt of steel job losses.
newsitem.headline: Krupp to take brunt of steel job losses.

text.p: German steel maker Krupp will face the brunt of the around 8,000 job cuts to be made when it merges its steel company with that of rival Thyssen AG, a state government official said on Wednesday.
Wolfgang Clement, economics minister in North Rhine-Westphalia state, said around 3,600 jobs at Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG would be cut from a workforce of some 5,700 at the Dortmund-based steel works.
He said Krupp and Thyssen had pledged to create around 1,300 jobs in Dortmund in other areas to limit the total number of job cuts in the city, but gave no details.

Earlier, Ekkehard Schulz, head of Thyssen's steel company, Thyssen Stahl AG, said that of the around 8,000 job cuts planned, 4,000 had been agreed previously in restructuring in areas where the two companies already co-operate.
The additional 4,000 job cuts were the only redundancies directly related to the merger with Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG.
Clement added that of the total job cuts planned, around 1,000 would be in administration.
The two companies would probably issue a hiring freeze and offer voluntary severance packages to accelerate workforce reductions, he said.
He added that more detailed issues such as the future of particular manufacturing sites or coke requirements had not been finalised yet.
The companies have said they would work out the details of the steel merger over the next four weeks.
